title: Birsa Munda
summary: Born in Ulihatu village, Khunti district, he led the Ulgulan, a Munda rebellion he declared on 24 December 1899. Thousands gathered at Dombari Buru hill on 9 January 1900; DD News cites a newspaper report of around 400 killed. Arrested in February 1900, he died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900; India now marks his birthday as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

uncertainty.note: Dates are given to the day by DD News.

where.modern_name: Ulihatu, Khunti district, Jharkhand, India (pinned to his birthplace village, the centre of the Khunti-area Ulgulan; Dombari Buru is a hill near Tamar and he died in Ranchi)
where.historical_name: Ulihatu, Chota Nagpur region, British India

importance.justification: Led the 1899-1900 Ulgulan rebellion; his birth anniversary is a national observance in India.

audience_note: Describes a violent suppression of a rebellion and a death in custody.

sources.title: Who was Birsa Munda, whose Ulgulan declared the end of British rule in Jharkhand?
PM inaugurates Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Park cum Freedom Fighter Museum at Ranchi on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

reviewer_note: Government sources (PIB, DD News) used; no Munda community or museum text was reachable. Circumstances of his death are described as mysterious by DD News. The 400 figure is a 1900 newspaper report cited by DD News. Pin is the birthplace village; the movement ranged across the region.
